item.title: Apartment complex at demolished shop site given the green light
item.description: Ashfield District Council’s plans for an apartment complex on Ellis Street have been approved by the Planning Committee. The site of the now-demolished factory shop will welcome a modern three-storey apartment complex featuring 20 homes and a flexible ground-floor space, bringing desirable town centre living to Kirkby. item.title: Rushcliffe: Cash can still be used for council services at local outlets
item.description: Rushcliffe Borough Council (RBC) has highlighted cash can still be used for council services at local outlets, even as under one per cent of residents use the payment method. item.title: Ruddington pub set for auction with planning permission for expansion and apartments
item.description: Prominent village landmark dating back to the 1860s to be offered at auction on 24 March through national property auctioneers Allsop, with planning consent for expanded hospitality space and nine apartments. item.title: Nottingham school stabbing: Police update as investigation continues
item.description: Detectives are continuing their investigation following a stabbing at a Nottingham school. Response officers arrived at Nottingham University Academy of Science and Technology (NUAST), in Dunkirk Road, Lenton, within minutes following a call at 1.36pm on Thursday (5 March). item.title: Police announce high-visibility patrols around schools after stabbing and School Wars posts
item.description: High-visibility patrols will be operating across some of Nottingham’s schools and colleges to offer reassurance to parents and pupils. item.title: Arrests after driver crashes during police pursuit
item.description: Two men were arrested after a driver lost control and crashed after fleeing from police. Officers began following a Fiat Punto at about 9pm on Monday 2 March when its driver was spotted turning recklessly onto Ollerton Road near Worksop. item.title: Council announces 96% decrease in number of homeless families living in hotels
item.description: Nottingham City Council announced today that, for 13 consecutive weeks, no homeless family in the city has had to stay in emergency hotel accommodation for more than six weeks. In January 2024, there were over 130 families living in hotels as temporary accommodation in Nottingham. By January 2025, this was reduced to just under 50 […]
